The product of the driver, also in Mexico, where the unpopulated PCB, known as NEMA grade FR4, is placed into the circuit board loading machine. A stencil is applied to the unpopulated PCB and then painted with high temperature vulcanizing silicone (HTV); the holes of the stencil allow the HTV to be applied between the surface mount devices (SMD components) where the SMD components will be connected.

In Mexico, the unfinished driver after SMT is removed from storage and placed into the DIP plug-in machine which automatically inserts various electronic components to the unfinished PCBA. This process involves wave soldering, and then testing with the automated test equipment.
the completed light source sheets are robotically cut to a specified length into light board in Mexico.
